=== Kobayakawa Duel Rounds with Table Talk ===

Each player starts with 5 kamons. The centre starts with 10 kamons. The game lasts exactly 10 rounds.

Each round:
1. Deal. A fresh deck of 15 cards numbered 1 to 15 is shuffled. Each player is dealt 1 face-down hand card, which only that player sees, and 1 face-down reserve card, which nobody sees. One more card is turned face up: this is the Kobayakawa card, value K, and it is announced.
2. Draw choice. All players choose KEEP or SWAP at the same moment. A SWAP player discards their hand card face up, takes their reserve card as their new hand card, and looks at it. If you KEEP, your hand card is unchanged and your reserve card is not used. Every discarded card and who discarded it is announced.
3. Talk. Every player writes one short public message at the same moment, without seeing the others' messages. Then all messages are shown to everyone. Messages may say anything, including false claims about your card or intentions. Nothing said is binding.
4. Fight choice. All players choose FIGHT or PASS at the same moment. A player with 0 kamons must PASS (they are not asked). Each FIGHT player puts 1 kamon into the pot; a PASS player stakes nothing.
5. Resolve.
 - No fighters: nothing happens.
 - Exactly one fighter: that player takes their own kamon back. Their card is not revealed, and the centre pays nothing.
 - Two or more fighters: all fighters reveal their cards. Each fighter's total equals their card, except that the fighter with the lowest card adds K to it. The fighter with the highest total wins. If totals tie, the tied fighter with the lower card wins. The winner takes the whole pot. If the centre has at least 1 kamon, the winner also takes 1 kamon from the centre; if the centre is empty, the winner takes only the pot. Losing fighters lose their stakes.
6. All fighters, revealed cards, totals, the winner and every player's kamon count are announced.

After round 10 the game ends. The player with the most kamons wins; players tied for most share the result.

=== Kobayakawa Duel Rounds with Table Talk ===

Each player starts with 5 kamons. The centre starts with 10 kamons. The game lasts exactly 10 rounds.

Each round:
1. Deal. A fresh deck of 15 cards numbered 1 to 15 is shuffled. Each player is dealt 1 face-down hand card, which only that player sees, and 1 face-down reserve card, which nobody sees. One more card is turned face up: this is the Kobayakawa card, value K, and it is announced.
2. Draw choice. All players choose KEEP or SWAP at the same moment. A SWAP player discards their hand card face up, takes their reserve card as their new hand card, and looks at it. If you KEEP, your hand card is unchanged and your reserve card is not used. Every discarded card and who discarded it is announced.
3. Talk. Every player writes one short public message at the same moment, without seeing the others' messages. Then all messages are shown to everyone. Messages may say anything, including false claims about your card or intentions. Nothing said is binding.
4. Fight choice. All players choose FIGHT or PASS at the same moment. A player with 0 kamons must PASS (they are not asked). Each FIGHT player puts 1 kamon into the pot; a PASS player stakes nothing.
5. Resolve.
 - No fighters: nothing happens.
 - Exactly one fighter: that player takes their own kamon back. Their card is not revealed, and the centre pays nothing.
 - Two or more fighters: all fighters reveal their cards. Each fighter's total equals their card, except that the fighter with the lowest card adds K to it. The fighter with the highest total wins. If totals tie, the tied fighter with the lower card wins. The winner takes the whole pot. If the centre has at least 1 kamon, the winner also takes 1 kamon from the centre; if the centre is empty, the winner takes only the pot. Losing fighters lose their stakes.
6. All fighters, revealed cards, totals, the winner and every player's kamon count are announced.

After round 10 the game ends. The player with the most kamons wins; players tied for most share the result.

Each player starts with 5 kamons. The centre starts with 10 kamons. The game lasts exactly 10 rounds.

Each player starts with 5 kamons. The centre starts with 10 kamons. The game lasts exactly 10 rounds.

Each player starts with 5 kamons. The centre starts with 10 kamons. The game lasts exactly 10 rounds.

3. Talk. Every player writes one short public message at the same moment, without seeing the others' messages. Then all messages are shown to everyone. Messages may say anything, including false claims about your card or intentions. Nothing said is binding.

=== Kobayakawa Duel Rounds with Table Talk ===

Each player starts with 5 kamons. The centre starts with 10 kamons. The game lasts exactly 10 rounds.

Each round:
1. Deal. A fresh deck of 15 cards numbered 1 to 15 is shuffled. Each player is dealt 1 face-down hand card, which only that player sees, and 1 face-down reserve card, which nobody sees. One more card is turned face up: this is the Kobayakawa card, value K, and it is announced.
2. Draw choice. All players choose KEEP or SWAP at the same moment. A SWAP player discards their hand card face up, takes their reserve card as their new hand card, and looks at it. If you KEEP, your hand card is unchanged and your reserve card is not used. Every discarded card and who discarded it is announced.
3. Talk. Every player writes one short public message at the same moment, without seeing the others' messages. Then all messages are shown to everyone. Messages may say anything, including false claims about your card or intentions. Nothing said is binding.
4. Fight choice. All players choose FIGHT or PASS at the same moment. A player with 0 kamons must PASS (they are not asked). Each FIGHT player puts 1 kamon into the pot; a PASS player stakes nothing.
5. Resolve.
 - No fighters: nothing happens.
 - Exactly one fighter: that player takes their own kamon back. Their card is not revealed, and the centre pays nothing.
 - Two or more fighters: all fighters reveal their cards. Each fighter's total equals their card, except that the fighter with the lowest card adds K to it. The fighter with the highest total wins. If totals tie, the tied fighter with the lower card wins. The winner takes the whole pot. If the centre has at least 1 kamon, the winner also takes 1 kamon from the centre; if the centre is empty, the winner takes only the pot. Losing fighters lose their stakes.
6. All fighters, revealed cards, totals, the winner and every player's kamon count are announced.

=== Kobayakawa Duel Rounds with Table Talk ===

Each player starts with 5 kamons. The centre starts with 10 kamons. The game lasts exactly 10 rounds.

Each round:
1. Deal. A fresh deck of 15 cards numbered 1 to 15 is shuffled. Each player is dealt 1 face-down hand card, which only that player sees, and 1 face-down reserve card, which nobody sees. One more card is turned face up: this is the Kobayakawa card, value K, and it is announced.
2. Draw choice. All players choose KEEP or SWAP at the same moment. A SWAP player discards their hand card face up, takes their reserve card as their new hand card, and looks at it. If you KEEP, your hand card is unchanged and your reserve card is not used. Every discarded card and who discarded it is announced.
3. Talk. Every player writes one short public message at the same moment, without seeing the others' messages. Then all messages are shown to everyone. Messages may say anything, including false claims about your card or intentions. Nothing said is binding.
4. Fight choice. All players choose FIGHT or PASS at the same moment. A player with 0 kamons must PASS (they are not asked). Each FIGHT player puts 1 kamon into the pot; a PASS player stakes nothing.
5. Resolve.
 - No fighters: nothing happens.
 - Exactly one fighter: that player takes their own kamon back. Their card is not revealed, and the centre pays nothing.
 - Two or more fighters: all fighters reveal their cards. Each fighter's total equals their card, except that the fighter with the lowest card adds K to it. The fighter with the highest total wins. If totals tie, the tied fighter with the lower card wins. The winner takes the whole pot. If the centre has at least 1 kamon, the winner also takes 1 kamon from the centre; if the centre is empty, the winner takes only the pot. Losing fighters lose their stakes.
6. All fighters, revealed cards, totals, the winner and every player's kamon count are announced.

After round 10 the game ends. The player with the most kamons wins; players tied for most share the result.

=== Kobayakawa Duel Rounds with Table Talk ===

Each player starts with 5 kamons. The centre starts with 10 kamons. The game lasts exactly 10 rounds.

Each round:
1. Deal. A fresh deck of 15 cards numbered 1 to 15 is shuffled. Each player is dealt 1 face-down hand card, which only that player sees, and 1 face-down reserve card, which nobody sees. One more card is turned face up: this is the Kobayakawa card, value K, and it is announced.
2. Draw choice. All players choose KEEP or SWAP at the same moment. A SWAP player discards their hand card face up, takes their reserve card as their new hand card, and looks at it. If you KEEP, your hand card is unchanged and your reserve card is not used. Every discarded card and who discarded it is announced.
3. Talk. Every player writes one short public message at the same moment, without seeing the others' messages. Then all messages are shown to everyone. Messages may say anything, including false claims about your card or intentions. Nothing said is binding.
4. Fight choice. All players choose FIGHT or PASS at the same moment. A player with 0 kamons must PASS (they are not asked). Each FIGHT player puts 1 kamon into the pot; a PASS player stakes nothing.
5. Resolve.
 - No fighters: nothing happens.
 - Exactly one fighter: that player takes their own kamon back. Their card is not revealed, and the centre pays nothing.
 - Two or more fighters: all fighters reveal their cards. Each fighter's total equals their card, except that the fighter with the lowest card adds K to it. The fighter with the highest total wins. If totals tie, the tied fighter with the lower card wins. The winner takes the whole pot. If the centre has at least 1 kamon, the winner also takes 1 kamon from the centre; if the centre is empty, the winner takes only the pot. Losing fighters lose their stakes.
6. All fighters, revealed cards, totals, the winner and every player's kamon count are announced.

After round 10 the game ends. The player with the most kamons wins; players tied for most share the result.

Each player starts with 5 kamons. The centre starts with 10 kamons. The game lasts exactly 10 rounds.

2. Draw choice. All players choose KEEP or SWAP at the same moment. A SWAP player discards their hand card face up, takes their reserve card as their new hand card, and looks at it. If you KEEP, your hand card is unchanged and your reserve card is not used. Every discarded card and who discarded it is announced.
3. Talk. Every player writes one short public message at the same moment, without seeing the others' messages. Then all messages are shown to everyone. Messages may say anything, including false claims about your card or intentions. Nothing said is binding.
4. Fight choice. All players choose FIGHT or PASS at the same moment. A player with 0 kamons must PASS (they are not asked). Each FIGHT player puts 1 kamon into the pot; a PASS player stakes nothing.
5. Resolve.

If the centre has at least 1 kamon, the winner also takes 1 kamon from the centre; if the centre is empty, the winner takes only the pot. Losing fighters lose their stakes.
6. All fighters, revealed cards, totals, the winner and every player's kamon count are announced.

Each player starts with 5 kamons. The centre starts with 10 kamons. The game lasts exactly 10 rounds.

Each round:

2. Draw choice. All players choose KEEP or SWAP at the same moment. A SWAP player discards their hand card face up, takes their reserve card as their new hand card, and looks at it. If you KEEP, your hand card is unchanged and your reserve card is not used. Every discarded card and who discarded it is announced.
3. Talk. Every player writes one short public message at the same moment, without seeing the others' messages. Then all messages are shown to everyone. Messages may say anything, including false claims about your card or intentions. Nothing said is binding.
4. Fight choice. All players choose FIGHT or PASS at the same moment. A player with 0 kamons must PASS (they are not asked). Each FIGHT player puts 1 kamon into the pot; a PASS player stakes nothing.
5. Resolve.
 - No fighters: nothing happens.
 - Exactly one fighter: that player takes their own kamon back. Their card is not revealed, and the centre pays nothing.
 - Two or more fighters: all fighters reveal their cards. Each fighter's total equals their card, except that the fighter with the lowest card adds K to it. The fighter with the highest total wins. If totals tie, the tied fighter with the lower card wins. The winner takes the whole pot. If the centre has at least 1 kamon, the winner also takes 1 kamon from the centre; if the centre is empty, the winner takes only the pot. Losing fighters lose their stakes.

records.system:
You are reviewing a game that has finished. You were not a player. You are shown everything: the messages the table was told, every move, and each player's private thinking at every move, which no other player ever saw. Each move carries the notes its game asked for, under their own names. The usual ones are:

  plan     what they meant to do over the coming turns
  reason   why they made that move
  predict  what they expected their opponents to do
  adjust   how they changed their own strategy because of that

Write two things.

First, a summary of the whole game as it unfolded: the turning points, the moves that decided it, and how it ended. Concrete: name seats, rounds and numbers.

Second, a review of each player. Judge their play, not their luck. For each one, compare their predictions with what their opponents were actually thinking and actually did: were they right, and did they see it in time? Did their adjustments follow from their predictions, and did their moves follow from their reasons? Point out their best and worst moves. Then score their play from 1 to 10, where 1 is aimless or self-defeating and 10 is sharp, well read and well executed. A player can lose and still score well, or win and score badly.

A player who gave no reasons, predictions or adjustments is judged on their moves alone; say that their thinking was not recorded.

Refer to each player by seat, and as "they".

THE GAME
Each player starts with 5 kamons. The centre starts with 10 kamons. The game lasts exactly 10 rounds.

Each round:
1. Deal. A fresh deck of 15 cards numbered 1 to 15 is shuffled. Each player is dealt 1 face-down hand card, which only that player sees, and 1 face-down reserve card, which nobody sees. One more card is turned face up: this is the Kobayakawa card, value K, and it is announced.
2. Draw choice. All players choose KEEP or SWAP at the same moment. A SWAP player discards their hand card face up, takes their reserve card as their new hand card, and looks at it. If you KEEP, your hand card is unchanged and your reserve card is not used. Every discarded card and who discarded it is announced.
3. Talk. Every player writes one short public message at the same moment, without seeing the others' messages. Then all messages are shown to everyone. Messages may say anything, including false claims about your card or intentions. Nothing said is binding.
4. Fight choice. All players choose FIGHT or PASS at the same moment. A player with 0 kamons must PASS (they are not asked). Each FIGHT player puts 1 kamon into the pot; a PASS player stakes nothing.
5. Resolve.
 - No fighters: nothing happens.
 - Exactly one fighter: that player takes their own kamon back. Their card is not revealed, and the centre pays nothing.
 - Two or more fighters: all fighters reveal their cards. Each fighter's total equals their card, except that the fighter with the lowest card adds K to it. The fighter with the highest total wins. If totals tie, the tied fighter with the lower card wins. The winner takes the whole pot. If the centre has at least 1 kamon, the winner also takes 1 kamon from the centre; if the centre is empty, the winner takes only the pot. Losing fighters lose their stakes.
6. All fighters, revealed cards, totals, the winner and every player's kamon count are announced.

After round 10 the game ends. The player with the most kamons wins; players tied for most share the result.
